intro: New Hampshire runs elections town by town and city by city, through the local town or city clerk, with the Secretary of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID, such as a driver's license from any state, a U.S. passport, a U.S. armed services ID, or a state non-driver ID. If you have no valid photo ID, an election official can verify who you are, and you sign an attestation of identity.

src.label: New Hampshire law, RSA 659:13 (photo ID at the polls)

check.text: New Hampshire Secretary of State voter information, including how to reach your town or city clerk.
check.label: Voter information

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: Set by each town or city. Polls open no later than 11:00 am and close no earlier than 7:00 pm.
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to request an absentee ballot
dates.detail: The town or city clerk must get a mailed request by noon on this day, or an in-person request by 5 pm. To vote absentee you need a reason listed in state law, such as being away on Election Day, a disability, a religious observance, or a work duty.

src.label: New Hampshire law, RSA 657:1 (who may vote absentee)

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Your town or city sets its poll hours. They open no later than 11 am and close no earlier than 7 pm. An absentee ballot must reach your clerk by 5 pm.

dates.label: Register to vote at the polls
dates.detail: If you are not on the voter list, you can register at your polling place on Election Day. You will need to show proof of citizenship, age, identity, and where you live. State law lists what counts.

src.label: New Hampshire law, RSA 654:7-a (Election Day registration)
New Hampshire law, RSA 654:12 (proof to register)
